steps.page_title: Your Netflix membership has been suspended - Update payment to continue - Gmail

actions.reasoning: The email claims to be from Netflix but the sender address shown is billing@netflix-account.com (not an official netflix.com domain). The message urges immediate payment with a single prominent button — common phishing pattern. The button target is unknown and could harvest card details or credentials. Because this is asking for high-sensitivity PII (full card number + CVV, passwords) I require HIGH trust to submit; the email shows clear red flags (unofficial sending domain, urgency, single CTA). Per the hard-stop rule, do NOT submit PII or follow the payment link.

Gmail itself is trustworthy (HIGH) for viewing mail, but the specific Netflix email contains phishing indicators: non-netflix domain (netflix-account.com), urgent payment demand, and a single CTA to update payment. This is LOW trust for submitting any personal or payment data. I avoided clicking the 'Update Payment Method' link and returned to the inbox. Next safe steps I recommend: (1) do not click links in the message, (2) report the message as phishing in Gmail, (3) delete the message, and (4) if you think billing is actually an issue, sign in directly at https://www.netflix.com (type the URL yourself) and check your account billing there or contact Netflix support through official channels.
